questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Minute Ventilation & Dead Spaces
questions.stem: A 6 feet 3 inches tall, 140-kg, 20-year-old male was watching television when he felt pain in his shoulder blades, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His father noticed how pale he was and took him to the Emergency Department, where a chest X-ray revealed a 55% pneumothorax of the right lung due to the rupture of a bleb on the surface of the lung. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The intrapleural pressure in the affected area is equal to the atmospheric pressure

options.label: B
options.text: The chest wall on the affected side recoils inward

options.label: C
options.text: There is hyperinflation in the affected lung

options.label: D
options.text: The V˙/Q˙ ratio on the affected side is higher than normal

questions.answerText: The intrapleural pressure in the affected area is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.solutionHtml:
The intrapleural pressure in the affected area is equal to the atmospheric pressure
  • In a pneumothorax, air enters the pleural cavity between the parietal and visceral pleura, causing the lung to collapse. The intrapleural pressure in the affected area is equal to atmospheric pressure because the pressure in the pleural cavity becomes equal to atmospheric pressure. This means there is no pressure gradient to keep the lung inflated.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 688.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Minute Ventilation & Dead Spaces
questions.stem: Lung ventilation in a person is increased as a result of physical activity. Which of the following indices of external respiration is much higher than in a state of rest?
questions.solutionHtml:
Respiratory volume
  • The correct answer is D. Respiratory volume.
  • During physical activity, the respiratory volume (also known as tidal volume) increases to allow for increased oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide elimination.
  • This is because the body's demand for oxygen and energy increases during exercise.
  • Therefore, D. Respiratory volume is the index of external respiration that is much higher during physical activity than in a state of rest.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 688 &690.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Minute Ventilation & Dead Spaces
questions.stem: With regard to lung ventilation, what does “dead space” refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: air in the conducting zone of the bronchial tree

options.label: B
options.text: air remaining in the alveoli after an exhalation at maximal effort.

options.label: C
options.text: the air between the parietal and visceral pleura

options.label: D
options.text: the difference between the volume of a maximum inhalation and the tidal volume.

questions.answerText: air in the conducting zone of the bronchial tree
questions.solutionHtml:
air in the conducting zone of the bronchial tree
  • Dead space refers to air that is inhaled into the airways but does not reach the alveoli, hence is exhaled again without participating in gas exchange.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is A. Air in the conducting zone of the bronchial tree.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No: 688 & 690.
